_comment: Ported verbatim from FX in Parlour v23.dc.html (line ~1054). 'on' is trait (reader passives + relics + marks, checked via has(fx)), sign (sitter denial rules) or job (sitter job passives). 't' is the canonical sentence; relic/mark card text is generated from it, sign/job prose stays hand-written in signs.json/jobs.json but should not drift from this line.

white.t: The first card with no element restores +2.

turn.t: Every sitter stays three readings longer.

pierce.t: The first 4 of every reading goes straight through denial, and restores +3 more when there is none left to pierce.

perOwn.t: Each card of your element restores +1 for every other one.

serpent.t: Your element turns to the next one every reading.

mutefirst.t: The first card of every reading restores nothing.

minthree.t: A reading of fewer than three cards restores nothing at all.

lasthalf.t: Whatever you speak last restores half.

shield.t: A wall holds off the first points of every reading. Whatever it holds off is worn away, but it thickens 3 again after every one.

norepeat.t: A sign already spoken in this reading restores nothing the second time.

deadel.t: One element restores nothing at their table.

steal.t: One card leaves your hand at random before every reading.

halfown.t: Cards of their own sign restore half.

energydown.t: You have one less energy every reading.

halfbest.t: Whatever your best card restores is halved.

nobonus.t: No card pays its condition — nothing for opening, closing or following.

tide.t: Nothing is held off the first reading, and the wall thickens 4 after every one.

deal1.t: You draw one more card every reading.

steady3.t: Saying the same sign twice in a row restores +3.

free1.t: Your first reading deals two more cards.

tax2.t: One card fewer in every hand.

_denial_wall_comment: NOT in the source — added during the port, see docs/PORTING_NOTES.md 'Taurus and Virgo'. denial_shield says how much a wall thickens by each reading; this says whether it is worn down in the meantime, and how far it may go. 'drain': true means whatever the wall absorbed this reading is gone from it, so a wall is a buffer to break through rather than a toll charged again every reading. 'cap' is a multiple of the sitter's base denial the wall may never exceed (0 = no ceiling). An fx absent from this table behaves as {drain: false, cap: 0} — the source's behaviour — so a mod adding its own wall fx needs no entry here unless it wants these rules.
_fx_amount_comment: HOW BIG each reader trait is. The mechanic lives in autoload/Rules.gd; the SIZE of it lives here, so a balance pass is a data change the author can read and revert in one file rather than a hunt for magic numbers in the engine. Every one of these was a literal in Rules.gd until the readers were measured against each other and found to run from 14% to 94% at the same point in a run (tests/balance_sim.gd). A trait with no `amount` here falls back to the number the engine was written with, so a mod adding a trait needs no entry.
